hypotheses.justification: Keep hX and split on XR. For XR > 0, use the existing proof. If XR = 0, both radii vanish: division by zero, Real.log_zero and OutgoingSchedule.sigma_zero make the heat multiplier 1; TerminalCompensation.correction_support makes the correction at 0 vanish. If XR < 0, X / patchRadius F XR < 0, so correction_support again makes the patch increment zero. Put y = Real.log (X / XR) and s = HeatTailEdit.switchStart F.data. Real.log_div and Real.log_mul require only nonzero arguments and give log (X / switchRadius F XR) = y - s. If y ≤ s, sigma_zero makes the multiplier 1. Otherwise U vanishes by Profile.logU_after, since core.endpoint ≤ s, as established in the proof of pulseEnd_le_switch. Thus the heat contribution also preserves E*U.

Keep hXR and use the existing proof for X > 0. At X = 0, Real.log_zero and OutgoingSchedule.sigma_zero make the heat multiplier 1, while TerminalCompensation.correction_support forces the correction at 0 to vanish. For X < 0, the patch coordinate is negative, so correction_support makes the patch increment zero. Set y = Real.log (X / XR) and s = HeatTailEdit.switchStart F.data. The sign-independent Real.log_div and Real.log_mul give log (X / switchRadius F XR) = y - s. When y ≤ s, sigma_zero makes heatE equal OutgoingDilation.E. When y > s, Profile.logU_after makes U zero because core.endpoint ≤ s (the clock inequality established in pulseEnd_le_switch). These cases prove the same conclusion without hX.
